definitions.explanation: A person who has gone before and paved the way in a particular field, serving as a model or guide for those who follow.

examples.japanese: {先達|せんだつ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{教|おし}え→教え：01909_oshie⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{学|まな}ぶ→学ぶ：01987_manabu⟧。
examples.english: To learn from the teachings of predecessors.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{分野|ぶんや}→分野：03612_bunya⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{先達|せんだつ}たち⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{努力|どりょく}→努力：03490_doryoku⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦あって→ある：00006_aru⟧⟦こそ→こそ：12731_koso⟧⟦{今|いま}→今：00945_ima⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: It is thanks to the efforts of pioneers in this field that we are where we are today.

examples.japanese: {先達|せんだつ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{残|のこ}した→残す：01975_nokosu⟧⟦{業績|ぎょうせき}→業績：04873_gyouseki⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{引|ひ}き{継|つ}ぎ→引き継ぐ：12458_hikitsugu⟧、さらに⟦{発展|はってん}→発展：03561_hatten⟧⟦させて→する：00392_suru⟧いくこと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{私|わたし}たち→私たち：28351_watashitachi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{使命|しめい}→使命：11445_shimei⟧だ。
examples.english: Our mission is to build on the achievements our predecessors left behind and develop them further.

notes:
Composed of {先|せん} (ahead, before) + {達|だつ} (reach, attain). A respectful term for those who came before in a field or endeavor. Has a somewhat literary or formal tone.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {先達|せんだつ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{倣|なら}う→倣う：10395_narau⟧ (follow the example of predecessors)
- {先達|せんだつ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{知恵|ちえ}→知恵：03428_chie⟧ (wisdom of predecessors)
- {先達|せんだつ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{教|おし}え→教え：01909_oshie⟧ (teachings of predecessors)
- {先達|せんだつ}⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧ (as a pioneer/guide)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{先駆者|せんくしゃ}→先駆者：27682_senkusha⟧ — pioneer, trailblazer (more emphasis on being the first)
- ⟦{先輩|せんぱい}→先輩：01451_senpai⟧ — senior (in school or workplace, closer social relationship)
- ⟦{前任者|ぜんにんしゃ}→前任者：19225_zenninsha⟧ — predecessor (specifically in a position or role)

CULTURAL NOTE:
The famous opening of {徒然草|つれづれぐさ} (Essays in Idleness) uses the phrase {先達|せんだつ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦あら→ある：00006_aru⟧まほしきこと⟦なり→なり：09883_nari⟧ — "It is desirable to have a guide." This classical usage gave the word a lasting literary association.
